summary:
Verified on the current build, using the real Chrome GPU at the gameplay camera (52°, 28.5 m). One harness ran at a time. Runs:
- my own fog on/off A/B probe on FRAY and RIFT, with fog on and off in the same session and sim state;
- a pixel-mask variant of the reviewer's wall-foot probe on RIFT (fighter drawn flat magenta, no shadow, outline hidden);
- shot_map at the spawns, the set pieces and the edges of all three maps;
- an offline point-in-polygon check of RIFT structures against thickets;
- re-reads of the reviewer's value, structures, ambient and foliage reports.

**Confirmed at major (4):**
- **F1 greybox landmarks.** The Fallen Shaft drum, the Snap stubs, the Dawn Arch blob, the Belfry block and the near-black shadow slab are early SDF primitives built 2026-10-14. They stand next to Art 2.0 structures.
- **F3 fog of war.** Fogged ground displays at ×0.21–0.32 per pixel against the ×0.55 spec. The FRAY plate goes from luma 84 to 19 and the awning from 156 to 59.
- **F4 wall-foot occlusion.** Within 0.2–1.1 m north of a block, 12 of 12 spots leave the fighter under 50 % visible (median 0.08 and 0.18); at 1.1–1.7 m, 5 of 6.
- **F6 brush round towers.** The four side-lane Outer Needles stand inside thickets 4–7. That leaves about 19 m² of brush at each tower's foot, and the sim lets that brush hide the defenders.

**Downgraded to minor (2):**
- **F2 FRAY.** The hazy court and the bare stands are what map_fray_landmarks.md §2 and §4 specify. The real defect is the off-brief hour-stones: pale caps at luma 114–122, against the brief's basalt lit top at L* 20–28. That belongs to the same landmark set as F1.
- **F5 Dialwood crowns.** Every measurable item in the r12 M11 fix spec passes. WORLD.md specifies solid bevelled plates. What remains is polish: no painted albedo on the plates.

The minors m1 and m2 are confirmed. Small corrections:
- the spawn views show 11–17 % out of bounds, and what shows there is the boundary wall and a moss or terrace strip, not a raw seam;
- the 'straight seam' in the edge pans is that N–S boundary wall seen edge-on.

No blocker-class issue was missed. The Wicks in lane shots have rounded, domed hoods and no face.

gapStatus.id: r12 §4 fog of war ('matches': value ×0.55, saturation ×0.4)
gapStatus.evidence:
Reproduced with my own A/B in one browser and one sim state (`_harness/_reports/final_maps_vfy_fog_ab.json`, shots `_harness/_shots/final_maps_vfy_{fray,rift}_{fog,nf}_at*.png`, sheet `final_maps_vfy_sheet_fog_rift.png`). Per-pixel displayed luma ratio, fog ÷ no fog, at fully fogged spots:
- FRAY: 0.232, 0.28 and 0.296;
- RIFT: 0.23, 0.254 and 0.322.

The spec is 0.55 (tokens.json:303). A spot in vision gives 1.0, which is the control. FRAY plate box 1100,600–1300,700: luma 83.8 → 18.7, about L* 6, against the brief's ≈ 27. Fogged RIFT frame p50 is 10–15. Cause: `src/render/world_material.ts:84-91` uses 0.268 = 0.55^2.2, which ignores the tone map and LUT.

The two shape languages differ: Aubade spires against Serenade domes (`_harness/_shots/final_maps_vfy_rift_edge_at0.png` vs `final_maps_vfy_rift_edge_at1.png`). The plazas differ too:
- Aubade box 400,300–1200,900: saturation p50 0.03, grey;
- Serenade box 900,400–1500,1000: saturation 0.37, ochre.

The greybox off-map landmarks behind each base are F1. The grey Aubade plaza is m1.

findings.title: Base, rim and centre landmarks are early SDF primitives next to Art 2.0 structures; out-of-bounds areas are flat planes
findings.what:
All the landmarks come from `art/blender/maps/landmarks.py`, built 2026-10-14, before Art 2.0. At gameplay zoom they read as primitives:
- **In fight zones:** the Fallen Shaft drum in the Sunsplinter pit is a plain cylinder with two dark bands. The BRIDGE Snap stubs at the map centre are plain banded cylinders.
- **At the bases:** the Dawn Arch is a smooth beige pillow. The Glass Belfry shows as a smooth chalk block with one arch niche, because only its first stage is in frame.
- **Rim and north choke:** the noon stone is a plain slab. The Longshade shadow slab renders as a near-black featureless box with no visible chalk edge.
- **Contrast:** they stand a few metres from the detailed Art 2.0 Hourbells and Needles.

The camera's focus is clamped to [0, W] (`src/render/camera.ts:52`, `:142-145`), so out-of-bounds ground is on screen:
- **At spawn:** RIFT 8.5,55 shows about 11 % and BRIDGE 7,22 about 17 %. What shows is the boundary wall and then a flat moss or purple terrace strip.
- **Edge pans:** about 50 %.

Correction to the reviewer: the 'straight seam' is the N–S boundary wall seen edge-on from directly south. It is not a cut in the plaza mesh.
findings.evidence:
My reproductions, from `node _harness/shot_map.mjs rift --q high --nofog --name final_maps_vfy_rift_edge --at "8.5,55;161.5,55;85,66.6;55.3,28.2;85,4"`, the same for bridge ("7,22;78,22;149,22") and for fray ("32,6;7.3,24;32,32;38,13.5"). Shots under `_harness/_shots/`:
- `final_maps_vfy_rift_edge_at2.png`: Shaft drum.
- `final_maps_vfy_bridge_edge_at1.png`: Snap stubs in a live fight.
- `final_maps_vfy_rift_edge_at4.png`: noon stone.
- `final_maps_vfy_rift_edge_at0.png` and `final_maps_vfy_bridge_edge_at0.png`: spawn views.
- `final_maps_vfy_wallmask_rift_01_d0.6.png`: the black shadow slab at 87.75,16.25.
- Sheet: `final_maps_vfy_sheet_edges.png`.
- The reviewer's `final_maps_rift_edge_at0.png` (Belfry) and `final_maps_bridge_nf_at4.png` (Dawn Arch) also reproduce what they claim.

Sources:
- `content/maps/map_rift.json` art.terrain.landmarks: model `assets/maps/landmarks/*.glb`.
- `art/out/maps/landmarks/*.glb`, dated Oct 14.
- `git log`: commits 67bc09d5 and ff3db500.
- Brief: `_design/maps/map_rift_landmarks.md` §2.
findings.gauge: At gameplay zoom, every Summoner's Rift prop is painted and finished to the same level as its turrets. Out-of-play vistas are dressed scenery: Riot even brightened them in the 2014 update as 'not a gameplay space' (surrenderat20 2014 dev blog mirror). They are never a bare ground plane or an untextured primitive.
findings.fix:
1. Art 2.0 pass on the landmark set in VALE's own language, using structure_kit's painted albedo, ink edge and chalk edge light:
   - the Shaft drum and the Snap stubs first, because they sit in fight zones;
   - then the Dawn Arch, Lamp Gate, Belfry (its lower stage carries the read at this zoom), Lamp Dome, noon stone and shadow slabs, each with a lit chalk edge.
2. A 20–30 m dressed skirt beyond every bound, kept at L* ≤ 52:
   - RIFT: Dialwood terraces stepping down;
   - BRIDGE: the gorge walls and the far bank.
3. Replace the flat spawn ring with a low dais.
4. Optionally inset the camera clamp by about 4 m.
findings.files: art/blender/maps/landmarks.py, art/out/maps/landmarks/*.glb, content/maps/map_rift.json, content/maps/map_bridge.json, src/render/terrain.ts, src/render/camera.ts
findings.verifierNote:
Reproduced on fresh captures. The severity holds, because two of the pieces sit in the middle of fight zones and are on screen in ordinary play, not only on edge pans. Two of the reviewer's details are softened:
- the spawn out-of-bounds share is 11–17 % (not 14–20 %), and it is wall plus a strip;
- the 'seam' is the boundary wall seen edge-on.
I added the near-black Longshade shadow slab.

findings.title: Fog of war is about twice as dark as VALE's own ×0.55 spec, and inconsistent between materials
findings.what:
Fogged terrain displays at ×0.21–0.32 of its lit luma, against the spec's ×0.55 on the display. The shader assumes pure sRGB gamma: `vec3 fogged = ... * 0.268` with the comment '0.55^2.2 = 0.268' (`src/render/world_material.ts:84-91`). The Neutral tone map and the LUT then crush the dark end further.
- Fogged RIFT jungle frames sit at luma p50 10–15.
- The FRAY plate falls to about L* 6, against the brief's ≈ 27 (`_design/maps/map_fray_landmarks.md` §3).
- Landmark materials take a different path: the FRAY cart awning only goes to ×0.38.

Fighters' sight is a 12 m disc (`src/sim/vision.ts:24`), with no wall occlusion of sight. So a lone fighter's frame corners and every scouting pan show this near-black ground.
findings.gauge: LoL darkens and desaturates unseen terrain, but lane edges, walls and brush stay legible, so players plan through fog. Riot's 2014 update tuned fog for a clear edge, not for blackout. r12 §4 scored VALE as matching at ×0.55, a figure the build does not deliver. No LoL frame was re-measured, so the LoL ratio itself is unmeasured.
findings.fix:
1. Calibrate fog on the display. Either apply it after the tone map and LUT, in a screen-space pass that samples valeFogTex at the reconstructed world position, or solve the linear factor against the measured tone map + LUT response.
2. Route landmarks, ambient props and the cart through the same function.
3. Add a fog A/B gate to value_probe: ratio 0.50–0.60 on lane, plate and jungle floor, at both tiers.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced independently, with a per-pixel ratio instead of box medians, and the result is the same. The severity holds: the spec number is missed by about 2× and fog is on screen in ordinary play.

findings.title: Fighters standing just north of a wall block are hidden by the block and its canopy, with no silhouette
findings.what:
On RIFT, a fighter on walkable ground within about 1.7 m north of a wall block is mostly hidden by the block's lip and its Dialwood canopy. The block sits between the fighter and the camera, and nothing replaces the hidden body. Only the overhead bar shows.
- Structures have an occlusion fade (`src/render/structures.ts`); terrain and trees do not.
- `src/render/terrain.ts:1410-1411` accepts that a cliff hides 0.78·h of ground behind it. It only stops the crowns from adding more.
- 15.3 % of RIFT walkable cells fall in this band: 3.7 % fully behind and 11.5 % partly.
findings.evidence:
My pixel-mask variant of the reviewer's probe: `node /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sitskovich-Developer-forgeflow-games/4e79f165-d0b0-4b1f-a3d3-f4bc44cd631b/scratchpad/verify_env/wallmask.mjs rift --n 24 --out _harness/_reports/final_maps_vfy_wallmask_rift.json --shots final_maps_vfy_wallmask_rift`. The fighter is drawn flat magenta, with no shadow and the outline hidden. Visibility is the number of mask pixels with the occluders, divided by the number with cliffs, rock stacks and scatter hidden.

| Distance north of wall | Spots under 50 % visible | Median visibility |
|---|---|---|
| 0.2–0.7 m | 6/6 | 0.08 |
| 0.7–1.1 m | 6/6 | 0.18 |
| 1.1–1.7 m | 5/6 | 0.45 |
| 1.7–2.6 m | 0/6 | 0.67 |

The reviewer's diff-sum metric gave about the same.

Shots: `_harness/_shots/final_maps_vfy_sheet_wallmask.png` (four spots: head only, or nothing, above the lip) and `final_maps_vfy_wallmask_rift_*.png`.
findings.gauge: r06 §2 and §6.1 [30][32] record that Riot's 2014 rebuild cut how often terrain hides champions, and r06 item 8 asks VALE to 'minimize terrain that hides characters'. The reviewer's further claim that LoL keeps the camera-side terrain low was not confirmed by my search. It is plausible, but unsourced.
findings.fix:
1. Draw an occluded-unit silhouette after the opaque pass: a depth test GREATER against terrain and scatter only, then a 40–50 % relationship-colour fill with a 1.5 px rim, batched with the unit path.
2. Where a lane runs along a block's north lip, cap the lip and the crowns within 2 m of it at ≤ 2.2 m.
3. Acceptance: no walkable spot leaves a fighter under 50 % readable, counting the silhouette.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced with a stricter pixel-count metric (no shadow or colour-contrast bias), and the result is slightly worse than the reviewer's. The severity holds: about 15 % of walkable ground is affected on the main map, which is a gameplay readability problem.

findings.title: RIFT's four side-lane Outer Needles stand inside Needlegrass thickets
findings.what:
The north and south Outer Needles of both teams stand inside thickets 4, 5, 6 and 7. Each thicket is 23 m² round a needle of collision radius 1.1 m, which leaves about 19 m² of brush at the tower's foot.

The sim treats this brush asymmetrically:
- Structures count as occupying their thicket (`src/sim/vision.ts:104-106`), so the tower's own team always sees inside it.
- Defenders standing in that ring are hidden from attackers outside it (`vision.ts:130`).

The result is a free hiding spot for defenders at the tower's foot, and the base of the tower is cluttered with grass blades.

Cause: `_design/tools/map_gen.py:397` places the eleven-line tuft at polar(85,55,46,57°), which is (59.95, 16.42). The keep_out list at `:403-405` covers camps only.
findings.evidence:
An offline point-in-polygon check over `content/maps/map_rift.json` structures × thickets shows exactly these four inside: a_high/a_low/s_high/s_low needle_outer. Every other structure is at least 1.7 m outside any thicket.

Visual: `_harness/_shots/final_maps_value/value_rift_high_final_maps_lane0.png` shows the needle inside a curbed grass ring. `_harness/_shots/final_maps_vfy_wallmask_rift_13_d1.4.png` shows the same at 59.75,17.75.
findings.gauge: LoL keeps turret footprints on open ground. Its lane bushes sit between turrets, not on them, so tower dives and fights under a tower stay readable for both sides.
findings.fix:
1. Add keep-out discs of collision radius + 3 m round every structure to thicket_json(..., keep_out=...).
2. Move the eleven-line tuft back to the jungle mouth.
3. Regenerate the map, then re-run _harness/probe_maps.ts and value_probe.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed in the data and on screen. I also checked the vision rules: the brush gives defenders asymmetric concealment, so this is a gameplay fault and not only a visual one. Major, and a small fix.

findings.title: FRAY's hour-stones are off-brief pale caps; the boundary dressing is sparse (largely by design)
findings.gauge: LoL's out-of-play vistas are scenery that is deliberately lighter and non-gameplay. A hazed boundary is within that vocabulary. Obstacles in play are finished, painted props.
findings.fix:
1. Rebuild the hour-stones to the brief: dark basalt, chalk-lit chamfer, half-hour tick, lit top L* 20–28.
2. Optional, as a design ask rather than a defect: give the court some lampwright stalls or rope lines at L* ≤ 52, and add the low cloth awnings the brief allows on the stands.
findings.verifierNote: Downgraded from major to minor. The 'greybox stage' read rests mostly on the haze court and bare stands, and the FRAY brief specifies both. What is off-brief is the hour-stones, which come from the same pre-Art-2.0 landmark set as F1. The crowd and festival dressing the reviewer proposes is a new design ask, not a defect.

findings.title: Dialwood crowns show unpainted polygon plates (the M11 residual)
findings.evidence: `_harness/_shots/final_maps_foliage/foliage_rift_final_wood.png` (11 m) and `_harness/_shots/final_maps_value/value_rift_high_final_maps_lane0.png` (28.5 m). Canopy share is 14.1 % of RIFT High frames (`_harness/_reports/final_maps_value_probe.json` masks.canopy). The reviewer's acceptance metric for straight-edge runs was not measured, by either of us.
findings.gauge: r12 M11: LoL foliage is painterly but graphic, and painted edges hide the geometry.
findings.fix: Keep the plate language and add painted albedo per plate: vein strokes, a root-to-tip gradient, notched tips, cavity darkening between plates, and ±3 % hue jitter per tree. Keep the canopy value band.
findings.verifierNote: Downgraded from major to minor. The look is real, but it does not hurt readability. Every value and motion gate passes, and the solid-plate style is mandated by WORLD.md. What remains is polish, not a defect at gameplay zoom.

findings.title: Bases are outside the B5 probe; the Aubade plaza is grey and the Hourbell tops the value range
findings.what: value_probe.mjs has no base spot (`:279-303`). At the Aubade spawn the plaza is near-neutral (saturation p50 0.03), below the 0.17–0.40 ground band, while the Serenade plaza is at 0.37. The white Aubade Hourbell outshines the fighters: luma p95 225 against the fighters' 214.
findings.evidence:
imgstat on `_harness/_shots/final_maps_vfy_rift_edge_at0.png`:
- plaza box 400,300–1200,900: saturation 0.03;
- Hourbell box 1300,230–1700,700: p95 225.1, 22.6 % above 180.

On `final_maps_vfy_rift_edge_at1.png`, the Serenade plaza: saturation 0.37.

Fighter lumaP95 214: `final_maps_value_probe.json` rift_high.fighters.
findings.gauge: In LoL the ground stays tinted, and structures sit below champions in visual priority (r12 B5).
findings.fix:
1. Add base spots to value_probe.
2. Tint the Aubade plaza toward a cool chalk-cream at C* 10–14.
3. Cap structure chalk at about L* 80, keeping the lit accent as the bright point.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced on my own spawn capture.

findings.title: Camps and the Sunsplinter pit lack identity dressing
findings.what: Camp clearings are bare discs with ring flags. The Sunsplinter shallows read as a blue-tinted tiled floor with faint ripples and the flag grid dominating.
findings.evidence: `_harness/_shots/final_maps_vfy_rift_edge_at2.png` (Sunsplinter pit with the drum), `_harness/_shots/final_maps_rift_nf_at4.png` (Glasshorn camp). Brief: `_design/maps/map_rift_landmarks.md` §3.
findings.gauge: In LoL, camps and the river read at a glance from their props and water treatment.
findings.fix:
1. Add one low prop cluster per camp lip, at L* ≤ 46.
2. Soften the joints under the water with depth darkening and a refraction wobble, and add foam lines at the banks.
findings.verifierNote: Consistent with my capture of the pit.
